title: Gemini and Sights of the South
caption: The Milky Way and laser guide stars above Gemini South, Cerro Pachón
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site
credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way flows across the southern night sky above Gemini South, which is sending up its five laser guide stars. A large red patch in the Milky Way at the center of the frame is the Carina Nebula, which ranks among the biggest diffuse nebulae visible in our skies. To the left of the telescope, below the Milky Way, lie the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds.

Gemini South is one half of the International Gemini Observatory, which NSF NOIRLab operates with partial support from the U.S. National Science Foundation. It stands atop Cerro Pachón in Chile, a place known for its dark skies. Its advanced adaptive optics system uses the laser guide stars to reduce the blurring caused by Earth's atmosphere.

Constellations dotted through the Milky Way include Centaurus, Crux and Canis Major, which holds Sirius, the brightest star in the sky. The Magellanic Clouds are dwarf galaxies that orbit our own, making them our nearest galactic neighbors, and their closeness lets astronomers study their stars in detail.

understand.summary: A night-sky landscape photograph by Petr Horálek. No camera or exposure details or color mapping are published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the night sky would look fainter to someone standing at the site.

explore: Indigenous cultures of the southern hemisphere have known the Magellanic Clouds for thousands of years, and they also appear in accounts by early explorers from the northern hemisphere. The photograph was taken during the NOIRLab 2022 Photo Expedition by Petr Horálek, a NOIRLab Audiovisual Ambassador.
alt: The Milky Way flowing across the sky above the Gemini South telescope as it projects laser beams, with a large red nebula at center and the Magellanic Clouds to the left.
